They delay action, they offer process instead of principle, They wait for others to lead. But when everyone waits, the system fractures. And when those seeking to dismantle multilateralism act faster than those claiming to defend it, the consequences are not neutral. They are devastating. This is the danger we face— not just collapse, but consent to collapse through caution, avoidance, and the politics of low ambition. So where does that leave us? It leaves us here, with each other, with conscience, with courage, with compassion, and with community. Because it has never been governments who set the moral compass of the world. It has always been us, the people. The communities at the margins, the ones whose rights are first to be negotiated away and whose labor, care, and clarity hold this world together.
